title: Burst policy engine: eligibility + per-tenant/per-region limit evaluation
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Implements burst admission policy evaluation for Redwood Dedicated. This PR adds the server-side decision function and API surface used by routing to determine whether a tenant is eligible to burst in a given region, and whether the request is within configured hard limits (concurrency and tokens/sec). This is the core of ENG-4823 and depends on the burst config schema/validation work in PR #8421.

Motivation: Dedicated customers need contractable burst behavior with strict noisy-neighbor protections. We’re starting with strict admission control (no preemption) and deterministic decisions.

What’s included: Adds BurstPolicyEvaluator and a policy service handler that evaluates (1) feature enablement and tenant eligibility (Dedicated tenant + burst enabled + region allowlist), (2) per-tenant/per-region hard caps: max_concurrent_requests and max_tokens_per_second, (3) deterministic deny reason codes and a stable response schema for routing integration, (4) caching of config snapshots with versioning + explicit invalidation hooks, (5) unit + service tests covering edge cases (missing config, defaults, region mismatch, limit boundary conditions).

What’s NOT included (follow-ups): pool saturation gates and global circuit breaker (ENG-4828), richer telemetry dimensions + dashboards (ENG-4826/ENG-4827), routing behavior changes (ENG-4824), and audit logging (ENG-4833).

Key behavior details: Eligibility: burst_enabled must be true on the tenant’s Dedicated deployment config; tenant must be on the burst allowlist (pilot guardrail); region must be allowed by tenant config (explicit allowlist) AND supported by fleet topology. Limit evaluation: Concurrency is evaluated against the in-flight counter passed by the caller; tokens/sec is evaluated against a rolling window counter snapshot passed by the caller (v1 uses a 10s window; this keeps policy deterministic and keeps state in the data plane). Decision is a pure function of (tenant_id, region, config_version, counters snapshot). Deny reasons (stable): BURST_DISABLED, TENANT_NOT_ELIGIBLE, REGION_NOT_ALLOWED, LIMIT_CONCURRENCY_EXCEEDED, LIMIT_TPS_EXCEEDED, CONFIG_MISSING.

API: Adds /internal/policy/burst/admit (internal only) and a shared protobuf message BurstAdmissionDecision used by routing. Response includes decision.allow, decision.reason_code, decision.limit_snapshot (effective caps), and decision.config_version.

Caching: Policy service caches tenant burst config snapshots for 30s keyed by (tenant_id). Cache entries are versioned; if a caller provides a config_version hint and it’s newer than cache, we bypass and refresh. (We’ll wire control-plane push invalidation in a later PR; this PR adds the interface + tests.)

Test plan: Unit tests for evaluator across deny reasons and boundary conditions (exactly-at-limit should allow, strictly-over-limit denies). Service tests for handler schema compatibility and config cache behavior. Manual: hit internal endpoint with a sample tenant config + mocked counters to validate reason codes.

Rollout: Feature is behind the existing burst feature flag. No customer-visible behavior changes until routing starts calling the policy endpoint.

Refs: ENG-4823, ADR-0142 (strict admission control + cooldowns; cooldowns implemented later).

policy: implement admit handler + response schema (protobuf + JSON gateway)
policy: add deny reason codes + mapping to safe headers
policy: add config snapshot cache with versioning + refresh
tests: evaluator matrix tests (eligibility, region allowlist, concurrency, TPS)

chore: docs in code comments for routing integration contract
conversation:
Ethan Park (review): Can we guarantee decisions are deterministic across replicas? We should avoid any wall-clock rounding differences for the TPS window.
Jordan Lee (author): Good call. Updated evaluator to accept the counters snapshot window_seconds explicitly from the caller, and removed any time.Now() usage from the decision path. Added tests that ensure identical inputs produce identical outputs.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Eligibility should be explicit for pilot. Don’t rely solely on burst_enabled; we need an allowlist gate until contracts are in place.
Jordan Lee (author): Added tenant_burst_eligibility_mode with PILOT_ALLOWLIST as default; evaluator checks allowlist membership. Also added CONFIG_MISSING as a deny when config is absent, rather than implicitly allowing.

Mina Haddad (review): For routing integration, we need stable reason codes (not strings that might drift). Also include the effective limits in the decision so routing can set backoff guidance.
Jordan Lee (author): Switched to enum ReasonCode in protobuf; response includes EffectiveLimits {max_concurrent_requests, max_tokens_per_second, window_seconds}. Added a compatibility test for JSON gateway output.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please emit at least basic counters for allow/deny by reason. We’ll need this for early pilot debugging.
Jordan Lee (author): Added policy_burst_admit_total{result,reason_code} and policy_burst_config_cache{hit,miss} metrics (low-cardinality). Telemetry team will expand later.

Logan Wright (review): Watch cardinality: do NOT label metrics by tenant_id here.
Jordan Lee (author): Agreed; no tenant labels. Decision includes config_version for correlation in logs/traces instead.

Ethan Park (final): LGTM after the determinism change + allowlist gate. Please make sure routing can pass counters; add a note in the README.
Jordan Lee (author): Added integration contract notes and example payloads in controlplane/policy/README.md.

Status: Approved by Ethan Park, Kaitlyn Nguyen, Mina Haddad. Merged via squash.
checks: CI: build (pass); unit tests (pass); lint (pass); protobuf compatibility check (pass); security scan (pass). One flaky service test on first run due to cache TTL timing; fixed by using a fake clock and reran successfully.
release_notes: Internal: adds burst admission policy evaluation endpoint and deterministic deny reason codes for Dedicated burst capacity pilot.
